title: Sanctity of a Muslim's Life
arabic_text: عنْ [ابنِ مسعودٍ] رَضِي اللهُ عَنْهُ قالَ: (قالَ messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: "لاَ يَحِلُّ دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ إِلاَّ بِإِحْدَى ثَلاَثٍ: الثَّيِّبِ الزَّانِي، وَالنَّفْسِ بِالنَّفْسِ، وَالتَّارِكِ لِدِينِهِ الْمُفَارِقِ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ").
english_translation: From Ibn Masʿūd (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) who said: The Messenger of Allāh (ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wasallam) said, 'The blood of a Muslim who testifies none has the right to be worshipped (in truth) but Allāh and that I am the Messenger of Allāh is not taken lawfully except in one of three: The adulterer, a life for life and the one who abandons his religion and separates from the jamāʿah (of the Muslims).'
description: This Hadith discusses the sanctity of a Muslim's life and outlines the three conditions under which taking a Muslim's life is lawful: for the married adulterer, qisas (retaliation), and for the one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.
